title: Response completeness
summary: A completeness result: ready or gaps found. Every reviewer comment is extracted and traced to a response and to a change in the revised text with its location, or to a reasoned rebuttal. Checks disagreements, consistency across reviewers and the length limit (one page for most NIH resubmission Introductions). The corresponding author or PI approves.
notAssessed: Whether the scientific changes themselves answer the reviewers well enough (that is the reviewers' call)
notes: Link both the earlier and the revised versions so each claimed change can be confirmed; otherwise claimed changes are unverified.
The one-page check applies to NIH resubmission Introductions (three pages for some training programs; the NOFO can differ). Journals set their own limits.
NIH resubmissions: outline changes only in the Introduction; do not mark them up in the application.

inputs.label: The reviewer comments
inputs.help: Link the decision letter or summary statement with the reviewers' comments.

inputs.label: The revised text
inputs.help: Link the revised manuscript or application so each claimed change can be checked.

config.instructions: Split the reviews into individual points. Keep each reviewer's numbering; split a numbered comment that makes two separate requests into two items so none is lost.

fields.name: asks_for
fields.label: Asks for
fields.description: Whether it asks for a change, a clarification or an answer

config.question: Where does the response answer this comment? Quote it. Does it give the change and its location, or a reasoned rebuttal?

config.instructions: List each change the response says was made, with the location it gives.

fields.name: change
fields.label: Change
fields.description: The change as the response describes it

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.description: Section, page or line given, if any

fields.name: for_comment
fields.label: For comment
fields.description: The reviewer and comment number it answers

config.question: Does the revised manuscript or application contain this change, at the stated location if given? Quote it. Compare against the earlier version where both are linked.

checklist.label: Disagreements give evidence or reasoning
checklist.question: Does every response that declines a change give evidence or reasoning, and acknowledge the concern?

checklist.label: No contradictions between reviewers
checklist.question: Do answers to different reviewers contradict each other, or does a change made for one reviewer undo another's request? Name any.

checklist.label: No comments merged and lost
checklist.question: Has any comment been merged with another so that one of its points goes unanswered?

checklist.label: Thanks once
checklist.question: Are the reviewers thanked once rather than in every reply, without flattery?

checklist.label: Courteous, not defensive
checklist.question: Is the tone courteous and specific throughout, with no dismissive or defensive passages?

checks.label: Within one page (NIH resubmission Introduction; journals set their own limits)

criteria.label: Points answered
criteria.guidance: Were the points answered as asked, with changes you can find?

config.instructions: Read the response beside the original comments in the sources. Tie each weakness to a comment and a passage.

reviewers.label: Original reviewer
reviewers.brief: You wrote these comments. For each of your points, say whether it was answered as you meant it, whether you can find the change, and which answers dodge the question or answer an easier one.

reviewers.label: Editor or chair
reviewers.brief: You are the handling editor or panel chair weighing the whole response: are the authors' disagreements reasonable and evidenced, were conflicting requests resolved sensibly, and is the revision ready to go back to review?

config.instructions: Approve the response before submission, after resolving or accepting each gap.
